facts.text: The repository adds UFACTORY robot model support to panda-gym training and simulation tools for reinforcement learning
pybullet and panda-gym are prerequisites of the repository
The scripts add a sibling ../panda-gym checkout to sys.path, so panda-gym is external to this repository
Only xArm6 and xArm7 (with gripper) are supported currently
uf_gym registers each XArm6*-v3 id on import, with entry_point uf_gym.envs:XArm6{task}Env and max_episode_steps 50, or 100 for the Stack task
The same registration loop also creates the XArm7*-v3 ids, with entry_point uf_gym.envs:XArm7{task}Env and the same 50/100-step limit
XArm6Reach-v3 is registered on the sparse/ee iteration: the loop visits sparse before dense and ee before joints, and those two choices add no suffix to the id
XArm6ReachEnv is the entry class of XArm6Reach-v3
XArm6ReachEnv builds a PyBullet simulation, creates an XArm6 with block_gripper=True at base position [-0.5, 0.0, 0.0], and attaches a Reach task that uses the robot's end-effector position
With control_type 'ee' the XArm6 action has three arm dimensions, and the gripper adds one unless block_gripper is true; the action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0, shape=(n_action,), dtype=np.float32)
set_action clips every action to the action space before using it
An end-effector action is scaled by 0.05 m per unit before inverse kinematics
The target end-effector height is clipped at z=0
With the gripper blocked, the neutral pose is the six arm angles 0.0, -1.103210210442149, -0.5245520784266224, 0.0, 1.62760333106346, 0.0 rad and the end-effector is link 6
XArm6.reset sets the arm to its neutral joint values
get_obs returns the end-effector position and velocity, plus the finger width when the gripper is not blocked
get_ee_position and get_ee_velocity return the link position and velocity of ee_link
The test script creates XArm6Reach-v3 with gymnasium.make and drives it through reset, step, render and close

determinism.notes: the fake samples its placeholder goal from random.Random(seed) and is otherwise deterministic, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a state hash; the upstream environment's own seeding and PyBullet determinism were not run or compared

gaps: the checked fake backend is an analytic kinematic stand-in: it has no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction or actuator model; the upstream environment builds a PyBullet simulation (uf_gym/envs/uf_tasks/xarm6_tasks.py:201) whose dynamics the fake does not reproduce
timestep_ms is 0: the fake advances one discrete transition per tick and neither the clone nor the fake declares the PyBullet physics timestep, so no simulated duration is claimed
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, so ticks are not wall-clock seconds and no timing model is claimed

the observation is a flat placeholder vector (end-effector position, velocity and goal), not the upstream observation structure: the upstream class inherits its observation space from panda-gym's RobotTaskEnv, which is not in the clone and was not imported
the reward, the goal range and the success radius are placeholders; the upstream Reach reward is computed by panda-gym, which is not in the clone, so no reward semantics are claimed
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state
no physical xArm device is modelled and nothing in this package was validated against hardware

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
